cip_requirements.title: Source and Scope Inventory
cip_requirements.statement: Inventory existing event, provenance, memory, agent trace, proposal, policy, evaluation, graph revision, authorization, storage, worker, API, UI, and deployment contracts. For each candidate integration, record observed request/response/schema, durability, tenant scope, auth path, and tests actually executed. Assign `REUSE_VERIFIED`, `EXTEND`, `REPLACE_WITH_APPROVAL`, or `NOT_PRESENT`; gaps have owners and tasks.

cip_requirements.title: Typed Dependency Contract
cip_requirements.statement: Implement versioned artifact and dependency schemas from Section 3. Validate IDs, kinds, revision references, tenant consistency, semantics, timestamps, and graph-size bounds. Reject empty IDs, cross-tenant edges, missing revisions, malformed times, unsupported schema versions, and invalid self-dependencies. Unknown semantic fields are never ignored.

cip_requirements.title: Dependency Capture
cip_requirements.statement: Capture direct dependencies when EOIP creates each supported retrieval, agent run, memory record, evaluation, and proposal. Include source/graph revisions, evidence manifest refs, prompt/contract/model/tool/policy/ontology versions, evaluator/dataset version, and tenant/principal context as applicable. Capture inputs actually read, not inferred from query text. Incomplete capture marks the artifact `UNKNOWN` with reason.

cip_requirements.title: Durable Mutation/Event Processing
cip_requirements.statement: Use verified transaction/outbox or equivalent durable event semantics. A committed mutation cannot be lost if the process crashes before consumption. Duplicates are idempotent. Cursors and impact records recover after API/worker restart. If mutation and event cannot share a transaction, implement an explicit recoverable reconciliation protocol and pending state; do not claim atomicity or exactly-once delivery without proof.

cip_requirements.title: Change Classification and Provenance
cip_requirements.statement: Preserve source/event IDs, revisions, change kind, tenant, actor, policy context, valid/recorded times, causal correlation, and redacted digest metadata. Apply temporal ordering to late events; do not mutate current state from a late event without that policy. Reject/quarantine duplicate, malformed, or untrusted events; never permissively mark current.

cip_requirements.title: Bounded Impact Computation
cip_requirements.statement: Compute transitive reverse dependency closure for authorized changed artifacts at an explicit temporal coordinate. Return direct/indirect paths, roots, revisions, states, and completeness/truncation metadata. Traversal is cycle-safe and deterministic, bounded by depth, nodes, fan-out, time, and tenant scope. Limits yield `complete=false` and reason, never a false complete result.

cip_requirements.title: Independent-Support Analysis
cip_requirements.statement: For multi-source derived artifacts, determine whether a valid, authorized, non-retracted support path remains. Enumerate valid/invalid paths and assumptions. Do not keep an output current just because text/confidence is unchanged; do not invalidate independent support because one redundant source changed. Incomplete/uncertain dependencies yield `UNKNOWN` or `QUARANTINED` under risk policy.

cip_requirements.title: Temporal and Historical Views
cip_requirements.statement: Evaluate explicit `valid_at` and `known_at`/recorded-time coordinates compatible with EOIP bitemporal behavior. Distinguish current belief from historical knowledge. Historical views still obey current authorization, retention, hold, and deletion policy. API/UI label coordinates and historical/current/partial/reconstructed status.

cip_requirements.title: Authorization Revocation Fast Path
cip_requirements.statement: Access reduction, revocation, tenant change, or policy update must deny affected reads synchronously at authoritative boundaries; background processing is not required to stop disclosure. Re-key/invalidate caches by principal, tenant, and policy revision. Prevent stale websocket, MCP, export, and browser state from serving restricted evidence. Avoid existence/count/timing leaks beyond policy.

cip_requirements.title: Repair Decision Matrix
cip_requirements.statement: Each impacted artifact gets a deterministic decision: `KEEP_WITH_PROOF`, `RE_EVALUATE`, `RETRACT`, `QUARANTINE`, `PURGE_IF_AUTHORIZED`, `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`, or `MANUAL_REVIEW`. Record changes, invalid/current dependencies, surviving support, policy revision, decision-rule IDs, uncertainty, reversibility, required role, and side effects. Keep requires persisted proof; unknown never defaults to keep.

cip_requirements.title: Dry-Run Immutable Plan
cip_requirements.statement: Plan includes tenant, actor, event IDs, input/dependency snapshot, policy revision, affected artifacts, ordered actions, expected revisions, bounds, digest, creation/expiry, and completeness. Reject/recompute if revisions or policy change before approval/execution. Dry run cannot mutate source, graph, artifact content, or external systems; only an auditable plan record may be persisted.

cip_requirements.title: Approval and Execution Safety
cip_requirements.statement: Reuse proposal/approval only if runtime tests prove actor, tenant, role, plan digest, policy revision, expiry, and single-use binding. Human approval is mandatory for purge, consequential retraction, evaluation baseline change, and external reconciliation. Automatic in-platform re-evaluation/quarantine requires explicit versioned policy. No unapproved write tool; approval cannot authorize another tenant or plan revision.

cip_requirements.title: Idempotent and Recoverable Execution
cip_requirements.statement: Use stable action IDs and expected revisions. Replays do not duplicate logical memory/evaluations/audit/proposals. Persist states `PLANNED`, `APPROVED`, `RUNNING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED_RETRYABLE`, `FAILED_FINAL`, `CANCELLED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`; define bounded retries. Preserve prior state until mutation commits, support operator recovery, honor cancellation at safe checkpoints, and audit all attempts.

cip_requirements.title: Evaluation Before Reinstatement
cip_requirements.statement: Pin evaluator, dataset, prompt, model, tool schema, policy, and graph/source snapshot. Compare candidate/baseline on correctness, evidence coverage/groundedness, policy violations, abstention, safety, latency, cost where available, and domain metrics. Missing metrics are `UNKNOWN`. Reinstate only if all mandatory quality/security gates pass and evidence remains authorized. Model judges cannot be sole oracle for deterministic invariants.

cip_requirements.title: Evaluation Threshold Governance
cip_requirements.statement: Version, freeze, and assign owners to gates before candidate evaluation. Unauthorized disclosure, cross-tenant data, missing required dependency, integrity error, or unapproved side effect always fails. Domain thresholds may vary only within governed bounds. Baseline changes require actor/approval and dataset/evaluator digests. Never tune thresholds after seeing candidate results.

cip_requirements.title: Read-Time Lifecycle Gate
cip_requirements.statement: Every API/UI/MCP/export retrieval rechecks tenant, authorization, state, retention, and policy. `STALE`, `REVOKED`, `QUARANTINED`, and `UNKNOWN` artifacts cannot silently appear current or enter new agent context. Provide safe state and authorized remediation details. Apply freshness to new runs and memory recall.

cip_requirements.title: Retention, Deletion, and Legal Hold
cip_requirements.statement: Purge only under approved retention policy and authorized role, after legal-hold checks. Remove/cryptographically erase content and content-bearing caches as required; check graph, files, logs, indexes, exports, browser caches, backups, replicas. Keep only minimum non-sensitive audit tombstone allowed by policy. Unavailable store means purge incomplete.

cip_requirements.title: Tenant and Principal Isolation
cip_requirements.statement: Tenant-scope all records, edges, cursors, plans, receipts, queues, caches, exports, metrics with identifiers, and UI/API. Derive tenant from authenticated principal; caller selector requires authorized membership. Revalidate jobs at execution. Cross-tenant admin requires explicit scope/audit.

cip_requirements.title: API Contract
cip_requirements.statement: Provide authenticated, versioned operations for artifact freshness; bounded impact preview; dry-run plan create/read; approve/execute/cancel/recover; paginated impact/repair history; and isolated non-production benchmark run/report. Routes may follow local conventions but cannot weaken observable behavior. OpenAPI documents scopes, tenant binding, limits, idempotency, errors, partial results, and states. MCP remains read-only unless an existing proposal-only boundary explicitly applies; never expose repair execution as a read-only tool.

cip_requirements.title: Operational UI
cip_requirements.statement: Show change/version, impact completeness/bounds, artifact counts by state/action, valid/invalid evidence paths, temporal coordinate, policy/tenant context, reversibility, approvals, execution progress/errors, and receipts. Provide filtering, detail, pagination, authorized recovery controls, and truthful empty/loading/partial/error/denied states. No fabricated success or operational values.

cip_requirements.title: Performance and Bounds
cip_requirements.statement: All work is bounded and validated; caller limits cannot exceed server maxima. Initial profile: 10,000 dependency edges per tenant, 100 changed roots, closure capped at 10,000 artifacts, impact-preview p95 <= 5 seconds on declared reference environment. Access revocation blocks the next authoritative API read immediately without queue dependency. Record environment, graph shape, warm/cold state, concurrency, percentiles, and memory. Missing profile data invalidates measurement.

cip_requirements.title: Observability and Audit
cip_requirements.statement: Emit redacted metrics/logs/traces for event lag, impact size/completeness, repair outcomes/retries, gate failures, denied stale/revoked reads, queue age and purge completeness. Correlate with non-secret IDs and tenant-safe pseudonyms. Audit plan/approval/execution/cancel/retry/purge/baseline actions. Observability must not create cross-tenant leakage.

cip_requirements.title: Failure and Recovery Semantics
cip_requirements.statement: Define behavior for corrupt journal, unavailable graph/dependency/policy store, worker crash, duplicate/late event, clock skew, partial traversal, provider outage, invalid benchmark, and failed evaluation. Uncertain safety-critical impact denies/quarantines. Health distinguishes degraded/ready. Replay is bounded and cannot duplicate external actions.

cip_requirements.title: AMRB Dataset and Scenario Contract
cip_requirements.statement: Build a versioned, synthetic, license-pending package with schema, validator, deterministic seed, expected outcomes, threat model, and no customer/source data. Minimum scenario families: 1. One source corrected while independent support survives. 2. All supporting evidence retracted. 3. Source deleted with answer and memory descendants. 4. Permission downgrade after answer/cache creation. 5. Tenant isolation under colliding IDs. 6. Policy revision changes retrieval eligibility. 7. Ontology/schema change alters interpretation. 8. Prompt, agent contract, model, and tool schema changes. 9. Evaluator/dataset change does not mutate old result. 10. Backdated and late events. 11. Duplicate event and repeated repair. 12. Crash at each durable mutation/consumer checkpoint. 13. Cycle, fan-out/depth cap, missing edge, corrupted digest. 14. Legal hold/retention conflict during purge. 15. External action requires human reconciliation, never automatic rollback. 16. Policy/evaluation service unavailable; conservative state required. Each case specifies initial graph/artifacts, tenant/principal, mutation, expected direct/transitive closure, state/action, forbidden disclosure/action, and deterministic oracle. No expected outcome depends solely on an LLM judge.

cip_requirements.title: AMRB Metrics
cip_requirements.statement: Report per-case and aggregate stale/revoked detection precision/recall; unauthorized disclosures (required zero); closure precision/recall; false-keep/invalidation; independent-support accuracy; action correctness/idempotency; crash convergence; truncation errors; latency/memory/retries/queue lag/cost; and unknown-dependency quarantine accuracy. Include numerators, denominators, confidence intervals, scenario strata, exclusions, and every failure. Never average away security failures or hide skips. Compare only matching benchmark/evaluator versions and environment declarations.

cip_requirements.title: AMRB CLI and Reproducibility
cip_requirements.statement: Provide documented validate/run/compare/export commands using EOIP CLI conventions. Support fixed seed, explicit profile, bounded concurrency, no implicit egress, JSON and human output. Record benchmark/evaluator digest, source revision, redacted config fingerprint, exact command/environment, per-case outcomes, raw metrics, summary and receipt digest. Never connect to or mutate production by default.

cip_requirements.title: Community Artifact Safety
cip_requirements.statement: Prepare benchmark schema, synthetic fixtures, validator, runner interface, expected-result docs, contribution/security policy. Do not publish automatically. Before release, authorized owner selects compatible license, reviews dependencies/assets, privacy/secrets and IP disclosure timing, approves destination. Contributions must be reproducible and pass validation/security checks. Results are not product certification.

cip_requirements.title: IP and Invention-Record Hygiene
cip_requirements.statement: Maintain a private access-controlled engineering record of dated human-authored problem statements, diagrams, algorithm versions, decisions, contributors, experiments, commands/results and digests. No secrets/customer data. Distinguish human contributions from model drafts. Do not send confidential details to external models/repos/issues without authorization. Do not make claims about AI inventorship or ownership based on tool ownership. Counsel/rightsholder owns patentability, inventorship, assignment, filing, defensive publication, licensing and FTO decisions. Agents may prepare a marked technical draft only when requested; never file/publish or claim patentability.

cip_requirements.title: Documentation and Migration
cip_requirements.statement: Document architecture, state machine, schema, APIs, controls, operator procedures, deployment, retention/purge, backup/restore, replay/recovery, benchmark, limits and troubleshooting. Persistent changes require forward migration, compatibility, rollback or forward-repair, backup/restore and upgrade/downgrade tests. No migration required for optional ephemeral benchmark data unless selected persistence needs it.

cip_requirements.title: Traceability and Release Gate
cip_requirements.statement: Map every requirement/acceptance clause to executable scenario, observable, receipt and accountable package. Verifier rejects duplicate/missing IDs/clauses, absent JUnit cases, failed/skipped/blocked results, stale source hashes, benchmark mismatch, absent integration, and wrong scenario counts. A marker, test file, generated receipt or checkbox is not proof absent successful execution and revision/environment binding. Report `NOT_RUN`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, `PASS_WITH_EVIDENCE`. Engineering completion is 100% only when all mandatory clauses pass; release readiness is separate. Denominator changes require versioned owner approval and history.

items.text: WP01 Baseline and Traceability — the registry reports all clauses OPEN; baseline manifest is reproducible; the three unsafe helper behaviors are either reproduced or superseded by new runtime evidence. No implementation credit from test names.

WP02 Contracts and Transactional Storage — round-trip validation, invalid-input refusal, duplicate submit, two-worker CAS race, crash recovery, and projection replay pass on both required storage profiles. Add a clear partial local-only status while PostgreSQL is unavailable.

WP03 Identity and Epistemic Foundation — confidence-only promotion fails; copied evidence is not independent; circular support is rejected; real sources can independently support a hypothesis; permission revocation blocks reads and actions immediately. Preserve existing graph fact semantics during migration.

WP04 Canonical Actions, Checker and Approvals — ASPEII-E2E-05 passes with independent zero-handler-call evidence. Cross-language vectors agree. A successful adversarial model narrative cannot alter the checker decision. Formal proof support is an optional plugin contract, not a requirement to invent a prover.

WP05 Gateway, Actual Effects and Receipts — graph correction changes exactly the approved record once; altered/expired certificates never dispatch; crash after external commit does not duplicate effect; offline verifier detects changed metadata/outcome/chain. Restore cannot resurrect a consumed approval.

WP06 Real MCP and Connector Qualification — both MCP transports prove actual server interaction; unreachable endpoint fails; malicious redirect/schema change is blocked; selected real connector has an observed effect plus reconciliation receipt. A local HTTP mock is transport test evidence, not the selected vendor integration result.

WP07 Intent and Outcome Contracts — ambiguous intent remains draft; read-only investigation cannot become write remediation; passing child status cannot bypass a failed outcome predicate. Compare actual runtime result to frozen acceptance through a separate verifier.

WP08 Delegation, Grants and Recoverable Scheduling — ASPEII-E2E-01, 02 and 06 pass on real workers; partial/blocked tasks are visible; all child usage stays within root budgets. No unrestricted recursive execution or silent delegation escalation.

WP09 Human Review and Epistemic Challenges — a review timeout never becomes approval; false support cycles and conflicting constraints remain unresolved; finite stress testing reports only the tested scope. Existing test-file links alone do not advance a requirement.

WP10 Semantic Access and Grounded Builder — a real source probe detects an invented column; ambiguous concepts remain alternatives; browse/resolve returns only authorized records; draft initialization cannot silently set the active ontology.

WP11 Trajectories and Candidate Isolation — candidate evaluation cannot mutate the live semantic version; poisoned trajectories cannot change policy; duplicated traces do not inflate evidence or measured improvement.

WP12 Paired Evaluation — deliberately bad candidate fails; constant evaluator is caught; missing case produces incomplete evaluation; gains reported for each qualified model/domain rather than generalized globally. A new candidate can legitimately remain rejected; do not fabricate a passing example.

WP13 Publication, CTAR and Rollback — ASPEII-E2E-08, 10 and 11 pass, including independent surviving support and model-specific qualification. Neural predictions never become facts through publication alone.
WP14 HTTP, CLI and Event Integration — actual HTTP/CLI/MCP paths agree on scope and outcomes; changed-payload idempotency conflicts; no public path can dispatch with arbitrary approval strings.

WP15 Integrated GUI Workflows — no hidden approval error, wrong proposal ID, overflow, inaccessible essential control or false completion badge. Screenshots alone are insufficient: show real state changes and denied effects through independent backend observations.

WP16 Independent Evaluation and Adversarial Harness — harness fails when a meaningful invariant is intentionally violated; all applicable 16 scenarios have reproducible results. Security failures cannot be hidden by passing average scores.

WP17 Operations, Deployment and Migration — actual install/upgrade/restore works; consumed approvals remain consumed; no secret/default development key in packages; resource/latency targets met or explicitly FAILED/BLOCKED for that release profile.

WP18 Final Release Evidence and Handoff — every required clause and cross-cutting gate VERIFIED on the actual release profile. Any gap yields a truthful partial release report, not a redefined 100% score.

Correction With Independent Support — Create two independent evidence sources supporting an agent result. Correct one. Verify impact and descendants, invalidated path, surviving path, pinned evaluation, and `CURRENT` only if all gates pass. Historical version is available only under authorized historical access.

Revocation Before Worker Processing — Create answer, cache, citation and memory from restricted source. Downgrade access, then request through API/UI/MCP/export/cache before worker processing. Each path denies or safely redacts. After processing, verify lifecycle/audit and no redisclosure.

Restart and Duplicate Recovery — Crash between mutation and consumption, restart API/worker, replay event twice. Verify one logical impact/action, correct cursor, deterministic plan, full descendants, and no fabricated success.

External Action Reconciliation — Invalidate evidence for a proposal referencing an external deployment/notification. Mark for reconciliation and require human proposal. No reversal API call; no claimed rollback success.

Full AMRB Run — From clean checkout, validate/run all scenarios, recompute metrics, bind source/environment, verify zero unauthorized disclosure/forbidden actions, export receipt. Skip/unavailable integration blocks full-pass label.

items.section: 2. Product constraints that bind every requirement

items.text: Configuration key `ip.public_release_allowed` (platform-level, default `false`). While `false`, CI MUST fail any job that publishes packages to a public registry, pushes to a remote whose visibility is public, or deploys public documentation that contains files under the IP module paths (§4.3).
items.section: 3. IP handling rules (apply to code, docs, packages and repositories)

items.text: Source files implementing Inventions 1–20 MUST carry the repository's existing licence header. If the repository has no licence header convention, add `Proprietary and confidential. All rights reserved by the rights holder named in LICENSE.` and record a DR.
items.section: 3. IP handling rules (apply to code, docs, packages and repositories)

items.text: Trade-secret material for Inventions 5, 6 and 9, and all tuned thresholds and trained weights for every invention, MUST NOT be committed to the source repository. Store them in the model registry (§14.0.4) with encryption at rest, and load them by reference. Repository files contain only default values from this document.
items.section: 3. IP handling rules (apply to code, docs, packages and repositories)

items.text: Code comments, READMEs and API descriptions MUST describe behaviour, not claim novelty. Do not write "patented", "patent pending" or "novel" anywhere until the owner sets `ip.public_release_allowed=true`.
items.section: 3. IP handling rules (apply to code, docs, packages and repositories)

items.text: Each invention module MUST include an `INVENTION.md` file (internal, not published) listing: invention number, requirement IDs implemented, algorithm IDs, the date the first working version produced an Evidence Pack, and the name of the person who directed the work. This supports the owner's dated invention records.

items.text: The status order MUST be a tenant configuration `warrant.status_order` (array of the six values). Only swapping `OBSERVED` and `ATTESTED` is permitted; any other order is rejected with error `WAR_INVALID_ORDER`.
`min(σ1, σ2)` and comparisons MUST use the tenant's configured order.
`warrant-service` MUST validate every warrant against the schema on write and reject invalid ones with `WAR_SCHEMA_INVALID` and the JSON-pointer of the first failure.
Warrants are immutable. A change produces a new warrant whose `parents` includes the old one.
Canonical JSON for hashing and signing MUST follow RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme).

Warrants for stored assertions MUST be persisted in the graph through the graph abstraction layer as a `Warrant` node linked `(:Warrant)-[:JUSTIFIES]->(assertion)` and `(:Warrant)-[:DERIVED_FROM]->(:Warrant)` for parents. Runtime-only warrants (propositions not stored as assertions) MUST be persisted in a warrant store with tenant-configurable retention `warrant.runtime_retention_days` (default 30).
`GET /warrants/{id}/lineage?depth=N` MUST return the parent DAG to depth N (default 5, max 20) in under 300 ms p95 for depth 5 on a lineage of up to 1,000 warrants.

The ingestion write path MUST create a warrant (operator class `OBSERVER` when `kgf:observerSource=true` for the source, else `HEARSAY`) for every new or changed assertion, in the same transaction or outbox batch as the assertion.

A one-time migration MUST create warrants for all existing assertions: existing `OBSERVED` → `OBSERVED` with grounds `source_record`; existing `PREDICTED`/inferred → `PREDICTED` with grounds `model_run` (model id `legacy` if unknown); anything else → `UNKNOWN`. The migration is idempotent and resumable, logs counts per status, and has a dry-run mode.

An assertion with status `PREDICTED`, `GENERATED`, `HEARSAY` or `UNKNOWN` MUST NOT overwrite or delete an assertion with status `OBSERVED` or `ATTESTED` for the same subject. It is stored alongside, and queries return both with their statuses unless the caller filters. Attempted overwrite returns `WAR_STATUS_DOWNGRADE_WRITE`.
Bitemporal reconstruction: `GET /graph/as-of?valid_at=…&recorded_at=…` MUST return the assertion set as it was valid and recorded at those times, with their warrants.

Every operator (tool, query template, rule, model, LLM prompt, human approval step) used by KGF features or agents MUST be registered with `operator_id`, `class` (`OBSERVER`, `COMPUTATION`, `MODEL`, `GENERATOR`, `HUMAN`), `version`, `owner`, `description`, `action_class` it can perform, and `approved_by`.
An unregistered operator invoked through the checkpoint SDK MUST be treated as class `GENERATOR` and its output status capped at `GENERATED`; an `OPR_UNREGISTERED` audit event is written.
Registering or changing an operator's class requires permission `ip.operator.approve` and creates an entry in the Warrant Review process (§15.1).
`OBSERVER` class is allowed only for operators that read from a source with `kgf:observerSource=true` or from the KGF graph assertions whose own status is `OBSERVED`. Registration validates this.

`warrant-service` MUST implement A1 exactly as specified, as a pure deterministic function `compose(operator, inputs, receipt_grounds, principal) -> Warrant`, with no I/O except reading the operator registry and ontology subtype relation (both cacheable).
**No-upgrade rule.** No code path may produce a warrant whose status is higher than allowed by A1. A property-based test MUST generate ≥ 10,000 random operator/input combinations and assert the rule.
Authority MUST never widen: for every composition, `authority_out.scopes ⊆ α_f.scopes` and `⊆ scopes_i` for each input. Property-based test as above.
Validity MUST never extend beyond any input's `valid_to`. Property-based test as above.
`compose` p95 latency < 5 ms in-process for n ≤ 50 inputs and ≤ 200 grounds.
`POST /warrants/compose` exposes A1 over HTTP for out-of-process agents (request: `operator_id`, `input_warrant_ids[]`, `receipt_grounds[]`, `subject`; response: the stored warrant).
`sasi-engine` MUST implement A2 exactly, using only local models by default. Model ids are configuration (`sasi.extract_model`, `sasi.embed_model`, `sasi.nli_model`).
Every generator call made through the checkpoint SDK MUST pass through SASI before its output leaves the rewrite checkpoint.
SASI output is a list of `(proposition, span, warrant)`; the UI renders spans coloured by status (§18.2).

Benchmark dataset `evals/sasi/laundering-v1.jsonl` MUST be created with ≥ 300 hand-checked items: supported paraphrases, unsupported additions, altered numbers, altered names, merged hearsay. Acceptance: on this set, precision of status inheritance ≥ 0.95 (an inherited status is correct) and recall of laundering detection ≥ 0.90 (unsupported propositions marked `GENERATED`). Report both on every model change.
Latency: p95 < 1.5 s for outputs ≤ 1,500 characters on the reference hardware recorded in DR (CPU-only allowed). Batch NLI calls.
If the NLI model is unavailable, SASI MUST fail closed: all propositions `GENERATED`, notice `SASI_DEGRADED`, alert raised.
The table above MUST be tenant configuration `warrant.min_status_by_action_class`. Changing it requires `ip.policy.admin`.
Every tool/operator that performs an action MUST declare its action class in the registry. Undeclared → treated as `IRREVERSIBLE`.

`POST /checkpoints/{checkpoint}/evaluate` (request: `checkpoint`, `subject`, `warrant_ids[]`, `action_class`, `plan_id?`, `principal_id`) returns `{decision: ALLOW|BLOCK|ESCALATE|ALLOW_WITH_DOWNGRADE, reasons[], warrant_out, required_tasks[]}`.
Every checkpoint evaluation writes a `checkpoint_evaluated` event (§19.2) with decision and reasons, and increments metrics in §16.
p95 latency of `evaluate` excluding SASI, lease validation and κ: < 20 ms.
Every answer produced by KGF (NL answers, reports, exports) MUST carry an answer warrant whose grounds list every proposition warrant used, and the UI shows the warrant (§18.2).

Provide an SDK in every language that hosts KGF agents or LLM features (at minimum the backend language). API: `with warrant_context(principal, plan_id): …`, `observe(tool_id, call)`, `compute(operator_id, fn, inputs)`, `model(operator_id, fn, inputs)`, `generate(operator_id, prompt, inputs)`, `handoff(target_agent, message, warrants)`, `commit(action, warrants)`, `answer(text, warrants)`.
The SDK MUST call checkpoints automatically; callers cannot bypass them except through `ip.warrant.enabled=false` (feature flag).
All existing KGF LLM features (NL query, query suggestion, report generation, entity auto-detection from JSON) MUST be migrated to the SDK. List each migrated feature in the binding map.
An MCP-compatible wrapper SHOULD be provided so external agents connected to KGF through MCP receive warrants on every tool result and must present warrants on write tools.

A verification task has: `task_id`, `tenant_id`, `proposition`, `warrant_id`, `reason` (`GENERATED_PREMISE`, `LEASE_EXPIRED`, `HALF_LIFE_DUE`, `DRIFT`, `LAUNDERING_AUDIT`), `suggested_observer_ids[]`, `assignee?`, `due_at`, `state` (`OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED_CONFIRMED`, `RESOLVED_REFUTED`, `EXPIRED`).

Resolution by observer call creates a new `OBSERVED` warrant with new grounds; resolution by a person with authority creates an `ATTESTED` warrant. Refutation marks the original assertion `valid_to = now` and creates a `refuted_by` link.
`GET /verification-tasks` with filters (state, reason, type, assignee, due before), `POST /verification-tasks/{id}/resolve` with `{outcome, observer_id? , note?}`.
A **laundering event** is any attempted warrant whose status exceeds what A1 allows. The service rejects it and writes `laundering_detected` with the offending operator and inputs.
The laundering audit job (§15.3) samples `audit.sample_size` (default 200) memory writes and handoffs per tenant per month and re-runs A1/A2 from stored inputs; mismatches are reported.
Each tenant has an Ed25519 signing key pair stored in KGF's secret store; rotation supported; public keys published at `GET /warrants/keys`.

items.text: `POST /warrants/{id}/export` returns a bundle: the answer or action, its warrant, the full lineage DAG, the graph snapshot version, model versions, data classes touched, the requesting principal's permissions at the time, and an Ed25519 signature over the RFC 8785 canonical bundle. Formats: JSON, and PDF with the bundle embedded as an attachment and a visible footer showing bundle id and verification URL path.
items.section: 6.9 Signed warrant export and replay (Invention 10, folded)

items.text: `POST /warrants/verify` accepts a bundle, verifies the signature, and optionally replays: re-runs the recorded queries against the recorded `as-of` snapshot (REQ-WAR-023) and reports `MATCH`, `MISMATCH` (with diff) or `NOT_REPLAYABLE` (with reason).
items.section: 6.9 Signed warrant export and replay (Invention 10, folded)

items.text: Exports never include data the requesting principal could not read at export time; the derivation guard runs on the bundle contents.

items.text: KGF MUST publish `kgf.graph.changed` events for every committed assertion create/update/delete: `{tenant_id, assertion_id, subject_id, change_kind, old_version, new_version, recorded_at, warrant_id}`.

Absent-capability rule: if the graph write path does not emit events, implement a transactional outbox table/collection written in the same transaction as the graph write (or in a compensating step for databases without multi-store transactions, with at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers). Database-native change-data-capture MAY replace the outbox per database adapter; record DR.
Event delivery: at-least-once, ordered per `subject_id`, end-to-end lag p95 < 2 s at 1,000 changes/s per tenant.

A lease is issued at the `retrieval` checkpoint for every assertion read inside a `warrant_context` that has a `plan_id`. Expiry = `issued_at + min(kgf:halfLifeDays of the assertion's type × lease.halflife_fraction, lease.max_ttl)`; defaults `lease.halflife_fraction = 0.5`, `lease.max_ttl = 24h`.
On `kgf.graph.changed` for a subject, all `ACTIVE` leases on that subject with `version ≠ new_version` become `REVOKED` within 2 s p95.
Leases are stored in a fast store indexed by `(tenant_id, subject_id)` and `(tenant_id, plan_id)`. Expired leases are swept every `lease.sweep_interval` (default 60 s).
`POST /commits/validate` (request: `action`, `warrant_id`, `plan_graph`) returns `ALLOW`, `REPLAN {affected_steps[], refreshed_assertions[]}` or `ESCALATE`.
The SDK `commit()` MUST call A3 for every action of class ≥ `INTERNAL_WRITE` and implement step 7 (partial re-planning) for KGF's own agents.
p95 validation < 50 ms for ≤ 500 leases.
Metric `kgf_ip_stale_commit_total{tenant,action_class}` counts commits that hit `REPLAN` or `ESCALATE` because of revoked or expired leases.

Demonstration scenario (part of the Evidence Pack): an agent plans a change using fact F; F is changed by another user before commit; the commit returns `REPLAN` naming only the steps that used F; after re-planning the commit succeeds; the audit log shows the full sequence.

`halflife-service` MUST implement A7, refit nightly (`halflife.refit_cron`, default `0 2 * * *` tenant local time), and store `(tenant_id, type, property?, model, params, h_days, n_events, fitted_at)` history.

When freshness of an assertion of a type with `kgf:criticality ≥ halflife.min_criticality_for_tasks` (default 3) falls below `halflife.phi` (default 0.5), create a verification task with reason `HALF_LIFE_DUE`. Rate-limit to `halflife.max_tasks_per_day` (default 200) per tenant, highest criticality first.
`GET /half-lives` lists current values with sample sizes and fit model; `POST /half-lives/refit` triggers a refit (permission `ip.halflife.admin`).

Unit tests with synthetic exponential and Weibull data MUST recover the true half-life within 10% at n = 500. On the seeded demo tenant, fitted half-lives MUST be within 15% of the planted values for every type with ≥ 100 change events.
`impact-engine` MUST implement the propagation exactly as specified, in prior mode from day one and in learned mode once a model passes its gate (REQ-IMP-004).

`POST /impact/propagate` (request: `changes[]{entity_id, change_type, properties[]}`, `max_hops?`, `include_paths: bool`) returns `impact_run_id`, `entities[]{entity_id, type, probability, hop, criticality, paths[]}`, `test_checklist[]` (entities of types annotated as tests or with `TESTS`/`VERIFIES` relations to impacted entities, ranked by probability × criticality), `summary_text` (generated through SDK, therefore warranted), `mode` (`prior` or `learned`), `model_version`.
Each response is stored as an impact run with its parameters and is reproducible: re-running with the same snapshot and model version returns identical probabilities (deterministic inference).

Learned mode is enabled per tenant only when the trained model beats prior mode on the chronological test split by ≥ 5 percentage points AUPRC and has calibration error (ECE) ≤ 0.1; otherwise the tenant stays in prior mode and the UI says so.
Performance: p95 < 2 s for |S| ≤ 10, H = 4, on a graph of 1,000,000 nodes / 5,000,000 edges (neighbourhood loaded through the abstraction layer with batched hop expansion).
Blast barriers and tenant boundaries are absolute: a test MUST prove zero probability mass crosses them.

`consequence-service` MUST implement A4 exactly and be called from the `commit` checkpoint for action classes `EXTERNAL_WRITE` and `IRREVERSIBLE`, and for `INTERNAL_WRITE` when `budget.apply_to_internal_writes=true` (default false).

`POST /actions/authorize` (request: `action`, `warrant_id`, `agent_id`, `plan_id?`) returns `{decision, kappa, budget_before, budget_after?, impact_run_id, escalation_id?}`. Budget debit and decision are atomic (no double spend under concurrency; test with 100 concurrent requests).

Escalations: `GET /escalations`, `POST /escalations/{id}/decide` with `{decision: APPROVE|REJECT|APPROVE_WITH_SCOPE, scope?, note}`. Approval creates an `ATTESTED` warrant for the action by the approver, then the action proceeds without debiting the agent budget beyond its current balance (approved κ is logged as `kappa_approved`).
`GET /budgets`, `PUT /budgets/{agent_class_or_id}` (permission `ip.budget.admin`), budget history per agent.
Metric `kgf_ip_budget_overrun_total{tenant,agent_class}` counts escalations caused by κ > B.

Demonstration scenario: a STANDARD_AGENT requests an action on a criticality-5 service with κ > 10 → escalated; approver sees the impact subgraph and approves; action executes; budget unchanged; a second, low-κ action is allowed and debited.

Protected-fact registry entries: `{protected_id, tenant_id, pattern, applies_to_principals (role/group/user selectors), except_principals, reason, owner, created_at}`. `pattern` is a graph pattern in KGF's canonical pattern syntax over types, relations and property predicates (e.g., `(p:Person)-[:SUBJECT_OF]->(:LayoffPlan)`), or a single assertion id. Entities, properties or relations annotated `kgf:protected=true` generate registry entries automatically.
`GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /protected-facts` with permission `ip.protected.admin`; every change audited.

`derivation-guard` MUST implement A5 and be invoked at the `retrieval` checkpoint for all agent and LLM reads, and for user-facing NL answers. Direct UI graph browsing by humans MAY bypass it when `dcg.apply_to_human_browse=false` (default true).
Absent-capability rule: if KGF has no rule engine, embed one that runs locally (e.g., an OWL 2 RL / Datalog engine), loading the tenant ontology's rules; record DR.

`POST /derivation/check` (request: `principal_id`, `session_id`, `candidate_assertion_ids[]`) returns per candidate `{decision, protected_ids[], derivation_ids[]}`. `GET /derivation/blocks` lists blocks with filters.

Benchmark `evals/dcg/inference-leak-v1` MUST contain ≥ 50 constructed scenarios where a protected fact is derivable from 2–4 individually permitted facts, and ≥ 50 benign scenarios. Acceptance: 100% of leak scenarios blocked within depth 3; ≤ 5% false blocks on benign scenarios.
Performance: p95 < 200 ms with |K| ≤ 2,000 and ≤ 500 rules.

Register every agent artifact: prompts and prompt templates, skills, tool schemas, agent memory records, eval cases, saved queries, report templates, dashboards, cached summaries and embedding indexes. Record `{artifact_id, kind, owner, version, location, content_hash}`.
items.section: 11.1 Agent-artifact registry and term dependency graph

items.text: Term extraction: for each artifact, extract references to ontology terms (type names, relation names, property names, enum values, synonyms/labels in every configured language) by exact and alias matching against the ontology's labels, plus embedding similarity ≥ `meaning.term_sim` (default 0.9) for free text. Store edges `(:OntologyTerm)-[:USED_BY {count, spans}]->(:AgentArtifact)`.
items.section: 11.1 Agent-artifact registry and term dependency graph

items.text: Re-extract on artifact change (event-driven) and nightly full sweep.

items.text: `meaning-service` MUST implement A6. Meaning release lifecycle: `DRAFT → IMPACT_ANALYZED → REWRITES_PROPOSED → EVALS_RUN → APPROVED → PUBLISHED` (or `REJECTED`).

APIs: `POST /meaning/releases` (from ontology version pair), `GET /meaning/releases/{id}`, `GET …/impact`, `POST …/rewrites/{artifact_id}/decide`, `POST …/evals/run`, `POST …/publish`, `POST …/rollback`.
Publishing a release applies ontology v+1 and all approved rewrites atomically from the user's point of view: either all artifacts reference v+1 or the release is rolled back.
Rollback restores artifacts and ontology to v within 5 minutes for ≤ 10,000 artifacts.
Metric: orphaned-term count = artifacts referencing terms absent from the active ontology version; target 0 after publish.

Demonstration scenario: rename a relation type used by 3 prompts, 1 saved query and 5 eval cases; release shows exactly those artifacts; rewrites applied; evals pass; publish; orphaned-term count = 0. Then split a type and show the human-review step blocks publish until approved.

Any consolidation (summarizing, deduplicating or compressing agent memory or KGF notes) MUST go through `POST /memory/consolidate` (or the SDK equivalent) which: (a) groups input propositions by status; (b) never produces a single output statement that combines propositions of different status; (c) produces output propositions each with a warrant composed by A1 from only the inputs it summarizes; (d) runs SASI on generated output; (e) creates verification tasks for any output proposition that became `GENERATED` while all its inputs were `OBSERVED`/`ATTESTED` (lost support).
Consolidated memory renders status markers inline (e.g., `[OBSERVED]`, `[PREDICTED]`) when exported as text for LLM context, using the template `metabolism.status_marker_template`.

Benchmark `evals/metabolism/consolidation-v1`: ≥ 100 memory sets mixing observed facts, predictions and hearsay. Acceptance: 0 cases where a consolidated statement has a higher status than its lowest-status input; ≥ 95% of input propositions represented in output (measured by SASI entailment).
`metabolism-service` computes the metrics above hourly and stores daily snapshots for ≥ 400 days.
`GET /metabolism/metrics?from&to&domain&type` and `GET /brain-health` (aggregate score and the per-region breakdown that Invention 1 contributes, §14.1).

Brain Health score = weighted mean of normalized freshness index (0.3), 1 − normalized toxicity (0.25), 1 − normalized verification backlog (0.15), 1 − drift hotspot density from Invention 1 (0.2), digestion-latency score (0.1). Weights are configuration `brainhealth.weights`. Normalizations documented in code and in the UI tooltip.

`branch-service` creates copy-on-write branches of a tenant's authoritative graph: `POST /branches {base_version, purpose, ttl}`. Reads on a branch see base + branch deltas; writes go only to branch deltas. Absent-capability rule: implement copy-on-write at the abstraction layer with a delta overlay store keyed by `(branch_id, assertion_id)` when the database has no native branching; record DR.

Simulated tools: every registered tool of class ≥ `INTERNAL_WRITE` MUST declare a `simulate` implementation that, given the call, returns the assertions it would change (no external side effects). Tools without `simulate` cannot be rehearsed and are listed as such.

`POST /branches/{id}/execute-plan` runs an agent plan against the branch using simulated tools, then computes `GET /branches/{id}/diff` (added, removed, changed assertions with warrants), impact (Invention 2 on the diff), κ (A4) and SHACL validation results.

`POST /branches/{id}/merge` requires an approval when κ > the agent's budget or any SHACL violation exists; merge replays the plan against the authoritative graph through the normal commit checkpoint (leases re-validated). `POST /branches/{id}/discard`. Branches expire after `ttl` (default 24 h).
Branch isolation test: no read of the authoritative graph by any other principal can observe branch deltas.
Used by Invention 8 (counterfactual path removal), Invention 11 (merge simulation) and Invention 4 (impact simulation).

Graph snapshot export per tenant, per level (instance, meta, ontology) into a columnar format (Parquet) with node table (id, type, properties encoded), edge table (src, dst, relation, properties), and snapshot metadata (graph_version, recorded_at, counts). Schedule `neural.snapshot_cron` (default daily 01:00 tenant time) and on demand.

Feature pipeline: type one-hot (or learned type embeddings), numeric properties standardized, text properties embedded with the local embedding model, degree features, recency features (days since last change). Feature definitions versioned.
Snapshots respect data classes: restricted-class properties are excluded from features unless `neural.include_restricted=true` for the tenant.
Use PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric (heterogeneous graph support) unless the repository already standardizes on another graph-ML library; record DR either way.
Runs on CPU (mandatory) and uses a GPU when present. Training jobs declare memory needs; jobs exceeding available memory use neighbour sampling (GraphSAGE-style loaders) instead of failing.
Chronological splits for every temporal task; no future information in training features (leakage test required per model).

Every model's predictions are warranted: operator class `MODEL`, status ≤ `PREDICTED`, grounds include `model_run` with model id and version. Predictions never overwrite observed assertions (REQ-WAR-022).
Embeddings stored per `(tenant, level, model_version, snapshot_version)` in KGF's vector store abstraction, with nearest-neighbour search.

Embedding alignment across retrains: orthogonal Procrustes alignment on anchor entities (entities unchanged between snapshots, ≥ 1,000 or all if fewer) before any cross-snapshot comparison. Alignment matrix stored with the snapshot.

Registry records `{model_id, tenant_id (or 'global'), task, version, training snapshot, feature version, hyperparameters, metrics, status (CANDIDATE, ACTIVE, RETIRED), artifact URI (encrypted at rest), created_by, approved_by}`.
Promotion `CANDIDATE → ACTIVE` only through the gate defined for each task, recorded as an approval. Rollback to the previous ACTIVE version in < 1 minute.
Absent-capability rule: if no registry exists, use MLflow (self-hosted) or implement the fields above in KGF's metadata store; record DR.

Compute embeddings for all three levels at each snapshot (instance: heterogeneous GNN self-supervised link prediction; meta-graph: types and relation types with instance-count features; ontology: concept graph with axiom edges).
Drift score per entity/type/relation-type: `d_v = 1 − cos(R·z_v^(t−1), z_v^(t))` with Procrustes matrix R (REQ-NEU-021).
Adaptive threshold per type: flag when `d_v > μ_T + drift.sigma × σ_T` (default 3) over the trailing `drift.window` (default 30 snapshots); minimum 5 snapshots before flagging.

Drift classification into exactly these classes: `SCHEMA_DATA_MISALIGNMENT`, `INGESTION_CONTAMINATION`, `USAGE_MEANING_DIVERGENCE`, `DEPRECATED_RESURRECTION`, `RELATION_OVERLOADING`, `OTHER`. Phase 1: deterministic rules (documented per class with the signals they use: SHACL violation rate change, share of assertions from a single new source, query-context shift, writes to deprecated types, relation-pair embedding multimodality). Phase 2: a trained classifier replaces rules when ≥ `drift.min_labels` (default 200) steward-labelled events exist and it beats rules on macro-F1 by ≥ 5 points.
Cross-level correlation: a drift event links to co-occurring drift at other levels (same type at meta/ontology level) and is scored higher when it appears on ≥ 2 levels.

Self-healing proposals per class (at least): constraint tightening (SHACL shape change), entity split, relation re-typing, ingestion rule amendment (mapping change or source quarantine), deprecation enforcement. Each proposal includes simulated impact: affected entities (Invention 2), queries whose results change (replay of saved queries on a shadow branch, §13), constraint violations before/after.
Auto-apply only when `drift.auto_apply=true` (default false) AND severity = low AND classifier confidence ≥ 0.9 AND simulated impact touches ≤ 10 entities; everything else goes to the steward queue.

APIs: `GET /drift/events`, `GET /drift/events/{id}`, `POST /drift/events/{id}/label`, `GET /drift/events/{id}/proposals`, `POST /drift/proposals/{pid}/apply|reject`. Events feed Brain Health (REQ-MET-012).

Demonstration scenario: inject 300 assertions from a new source that systematically uses `Server` for containers; heartbeat flags `INGESTION_CONTAMINATION` on `Server` within one snapshot cycle, proposes an ingestion rule amendment with simulated impact; steward applies; next cycle clears the hotspot.
Question decomposition into sub-questions, each tagged with ontology concepts (entity linking to types and instances), via local LLM through the SDK (warranted).
items.section: 14.2 Invention 3 — Metapath-attention question answering (Ask the Brain)

items.text: Metapath enumeration from the meta-graph up to length `ask.max_metapath_len` (default 4) between tagged types.
items.section: 14.2 Invention 3 — Metapath-attention question answering (Ask the Brain)

items.text: Metapath scoring: semantic-level attention between the sub-question embedding and each metapath embedding (metapath embedding = attention-pooled relation and type embeddings), with hierarchical attention over metapaths sharing prefixes. Select top `ask.top_metapaths` (default 5). Phase 1 may use a training-free scorer (cosine of embeddings + path-length prior) until a trained scorer beats it on the QA eval set (REQ-INV3-008); record the active scorer in each answer.

Candidate pairs: entities A, B connected within 2 hops, both with ≥ `causal.min_snapshots` (default 20) snapshots of embedding change magnitudes.
Granger test: VAR on the change-magnitude series with lag 1–3 (selected by AIC); F-test; Benjamini–Hochberg correction at q = 0.01 across all tested pairs per run.

Counterfactual check on a shadow branch: remove the A→B connecting paths, re-run the temporal predictor for B's next change; keep the candidate only if predicted change magnitude of B drops by ≥ `causal.min_effect` (default 50%).

Accepted pairs are stored as `(:Entity)-[:CAUSES {strength, lag, p_value, run_id}]->(:Entity)` in a separate causal layer (distinct label or named graph), status `PREDICTED`, never mixed with observed relations.

Explicit capture: SDK method `commit_to(promisees, statement, kind, due_at, about[], condition?)` and `POST /commitments` create a commitment in state `ACTIVE` with a warrant composed by A1 from the calling context (status of the commitment warrant = `ATTESTED` when made by a person, `GENERATED` when made by an agent; this records that the promise exists, not that it will be kept).

Implicit detection: at the `answer` and `handoff` checkpoints, agent outputs pass through the extractor (`POST /commitments/extract`; prompt template `commitment.extract.v1`, a registered GENERATOR operator, local model `commitment.extract_model`). Each detected promissory statement creates a `PROPOSED` commitment with its source span. The promisor agent's runtime must call `confirm` or `retract` within `commitment.confirm_window`; unconfirmed proposals become `ACTIVE` and a notice goes to the agent's owner.

Extraction benchmark `evals/commitment/extract-v1` with ≥ 200 labelled agent outputs (promises with and without dates, conditional promises, non-promises such as "you could…", reported speech). Acceptance: precision ≥ 0.90 and recall ≥ 0.85 for detecting promises; due-date extraction exact-match ≥ 0.85 on promises that state a date.

Authority: the promisor's authority scopes (A1) MUST include action `commit:<kind>` on the ontology types of every `about` entity. Otherwise the commitment is rejected with `CMT_UNAUTHORIZED` and an escalation is created for a principal who holds that scope.

Feasibility at creation: if `due_at − now < commitment.min_lead_time`, or the promisor already holds ≥ `commitment.max_open` open commitments, the commitment is created in state `AT_RISK` and the promisor and its owner are notified.

Lifecycle scheduler (runs every minute): `ACTIVE → AT_RISK` when remaining time < `commitment.at_risk_fraction` × (due_at − created_at) and no progress entry exists in the last quarter of the window; `ACTIVE|AT_RISK → BROKEN` when `due_at` passes without fulfilment; `CONDITIONAL` commitments become due only when their condition first matches the graph (evaluated on `kgf.graph.changed`). Every transition writes `kgf.ip.commitment.changed` and notifies promisees.

Evidence-based fulfilment: `POST /commitments/{id}/fulfil {warrant_id}` succeeds only if the referenced warrant has status ≥ `commitment.fulfil_min_status` and its grounds reference at least one entity in `about` (or, for `FOLLOW_UP`, a delivered message to every promisee recorded as an `OBSERVED` tool receipt). Otherwise `CMT_FULFILMENT_UNWARRANTED`. An agent saying "done" (a GENERATED proposition) never fulfils a commitment.

Commit-time conflict check: at the `commit` checkpoint, if an action modifies or deletes an entity that an `ACTIVE`, `AT_RISK` or due `CONDITIONAL` commitment is `ABOUT`, and the action's plan does not reference that commitment id, the checkpoint returns `ESCALATE` with `CMT_CONFLICT`, listing the commitments and their promisees.

Retrieval: when an agent works in a `warrant_context` whose task touches entities with open commitments by that agent, the `retrieval` checkpoint adds those commitments (statement, due date, state, warrant) to the context so the agent does not contradict them.

Transfer on retirement: disabling, deleting or replacing (new version with a different identity) an agent identity with open commitments is refused with `CMT_ORPHANED` unless a successor is named; then every open commitment is copied to a new commitment for the successor (`TRANSFERRED_TO` link, same due date, promisees notified) and the original becomes `TRANSFERRED`. Platform-level configuration MAY name a default human owner per agent class as successor.
`RELEASED` requires every promisee (or a principal with `ip.commitment.manage` on their behalf) to release the promisor, recorded with an `ATTESTED` warrant.

SDK `deliberate(question, options, participants, action_class, max_rounds?)` and `POST /deliberations` run the protocol: round 0, each participant produces a position in isolation; rounds 1..`dissent.max_rounds`, participants see all previous positions and may revise. Positions are produced through the checkpoint SDK, so every rationale proposition carries a warrant (SASI applies).

Isolation: in round 0 the runtime MUST NOT include any other participant's position, rationale or the deliberation's later state in a participant's context; the position records `seen_position_ids = []` and `isolated = true`. A detected breach (any other position id or its text hash present in the context sent to the model) voids the position with `DIS_ISOLATION_BREACH`.

Diversity: deliberations whose `action_class` ≥ `dissent.required_from_action_class` require ≥ `dissent.min_independent` participants with distinct values of `dissent.diversity_key` (model family, context source, or principal). Otherwise `DIS_INSUFFICIENT_DIVERSITY`.

Grounded stance changes: when a participant's option differs from its previous round, the change is `GROUNDED_SHIFT` only if its new rationale contains at least one proposition whose warrant grounds include a ground id that the participant had not cited or been shown in any earlier round and whose status is ≥ `PREDICTED`; otherwise `UNGROUNDED_SHIFT`. Restating another participant's rationale is not a new ground.

Minority report: on `decide`, if round-0 positions were not unanimous, a minority report is mandatory. It contains every round-0 position whose option differs from the decided option (even if the participant later shifted), plus any final-round dissent; a summary generated through the SDK (its propositions keep SASI statuses); and revisit triggers derived automatically from the entities in the dissenting positions' grounds (graph-change triggers) plus an optional date set by the decision owner. A decision without a required minority report is rejected.
Human approval view: when a decision feeds an escalation or approval (§9.2), the approver sees the minority report and the ungrounded shifts before deciding.

Revisit triggers: on a matching `kgf.graph.changed` event or date, emit `kgf.ip.minority.revisit` and notify the decision owner with the changed facts. The owner can record `POST /decisions/{id}/vindication {vindicated: true|false, note}` with an `ATTESTED` warrant.
Metrics per §16: dissent preservation ratio, homogenization index, ungrounded shift ratio, minority vindicated total; per agent and per model family.

Benchmark `evals/dissent/minority-v1`: ≥ 100 synthetic deliberation tasks over the demo tenant where the correct answer is held by a minority of round-0 positions (planted by giving one participant a decisive fact). Acceptance: the correct minority position appears in the minority report in ≥ 95% of tasks where it appeared in round 0; ungrounded-shift detection precision ≥ 0.9 against hand labels on 100 stance changes.

xp.title: Four status vocabularies
xp.issue: ASPEII uses OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/BLOCKED/FAILED/VERIFIED/STALE/DEFERRED; CIP uses NOT_RUN/FAIL/BLOCKED/PASS_WITH_EVIDENCE; IP uses NOT-STARTED/IN-PROGRESS/CODE-COMPLETE/EVIDENCED/VERIFIED/BLOCKED; Graph Neurons ledgers use COMPLETE/FAILED/BLOCKED.
xp.proposal: Each programme keeps its own vocabulary in its own ledger. The tracker stores one canonical state per item and shows the native label through the fixed mapping table (tracker section 'Status mapping'). The ASPEII↔IP mapping in aspeii-implementation-plan.md §8 is applied unchanged. Only the native 'done' value (ASPEII VERIFIED, CIP PASS_WITH_EVIDENCE, IP VERIFIED, GN COMPLETE) counts toward completion.

xp.title: Prediction / fact status models differ
xp.sources: Graph-Neurons-requirements.md GN-002; ip-requirements.md §5.1, REQ-NEU-013, REQ-VER-002; aspeii-reqirements.md §2.1, ASPEII-RQ-030.C04
xp.issue: GN-002 defines AssertionStatus OBSERVED/DERIVED/PREDICTED/REJECTED/CONFIRMED. IP defines warrant status OBSERVED/ATTESTED/PREDICTED/GENERATED/HEARSAY/UNKNOWN. ASPEII maps model output to HYPOTHESIS content. A neural edge needs exactly one stored status.
xp.proposal: Store the IP warrant status as the authoritative status and keep GN AssertionStatus as the neural-layer lifecycle field: GN PREDICTED = warrant PREDICTED (operator class MODEL); GN DERIVED = A1 COMPUTATION result (status = min of inputs, never above them); GN CONFIRMED = a new ATTESTED warrant by the human approver whose parents include the prediction warrant (REQ-VER-002), lineage retained; GN REJECTED = verification task RESOLVED_REFUTED (valid_to = now, refuted_by link). ASPEII classifies all of these as HYPOTHESIS unless independently verified. A neural path never writes OBSERVED (GN-002 constraint 2 and REQ-WAR-022 both hold).

xp.title: One neural implementation, two component names
xp.sources: ip-requirements.md §4.1, §4.3, REQ-NEU-010, §9.1 training; Graph-Neurons-requirements.md §1.2, GN-103, GN-104
xp.issue: IP asks for a `neural_service` module per component and trains R-GAT/HGT for Invention 2; Graph Neurons places the neural fabric in `packages/eoip/neural/` with R-GAT (GN-103) and HGT (GN-104) encoders. Two implementations would diverge.
xp.proposal: Bind IP component `neural-service` to `packages/eoip/neural/` in docs/ip/ip-binding-map.md. Invention 2 learned mode imports the GN-103/GN-104 encoders; no second encoder implementation. IP modules for inventions that are not encoders (drift, advisor, forensics …) live under `packages/eoip/neural/` subpackages named after the IP component.

xp.title: Model registry: MLflow / metadata store vs mlops experiment tracker
xp.issue: IP allows MLflow or the KGF metadata store and uses stages CANDIDATE/ACTIVE/RETIRED; GN-007 extends packages/eoip/mlops/experiment_tracker.py with a 'production' stage and seven promotion gates.
xp.proposal: One registry: GN-007's extension of experiment_tracker.py is the KGF metadata store named in REQ-NEU-032 (no MLflow). Stage mapping CANDIDATE=candidate, ACTIVE=production, RETIRED=retired. Records carry the union of IP fields (REQ-NEU-030) and GN gate reports.

xp.title: Promotion thresholds for learned models
xp.issue: IP: learned impact mode needs ≥ 5 pp AUPRC over prior mode and ECE ≤ 0.1. GN: ≥ CommonNeighbors + 0.05 and ≥ Rule + 0.05 AUPRC, ECE ≤ 0.10, anti-stub P1–P4, temporal validity, latency, security and explainability gates.
xp.proposal: Apply the conjunction: a model is promoted only when every IP gate and every GN-007 gate passes. Prior mode counts as the RuleBaseline for Invention 2. Neither threshold set is lowered.

xp.title: Two natural-language question endpoints
xp.sources: ip-requirements.md REQ-INV3-005, REQ-INV3-009 (`POST /ask`); Graph-Neurons-requirements.md GN-203, GN-704 (`POST /neural/ask`)
xp.issue: Ask the Brain (Invention 3) and the GN natural-language bridge both answer questions over the graph with different contracts (warrants vs citations + confidence).
xp.proposal: `POST /ask` is the user-facing route. GN-203 nl_bridge is the neural path of REQ-INV3-005(b) and must run through the checkpoint SDK so every answer carries a warrant. `POST /neural/ask` stays as the GN contract route and returns the same warrant id plus citations; both share one implementation.

xp.title: Embedding store ownership
xp.issue: IP stores embeddings per (tenant, level, model_version, snapshot_version) in the vector-store abstraction; GN-004 FeatureStore defaults to the graph-store sidecar and forbids a new database without a decision record.
xp.proposal: GN-004 FeatureStore is the single embedding store. It keys rows by the IP tuple (tenant, level, model_version, snapshot_version) and reaches the vector-store abstraction through an adapter; Procrustes matrices (REQ-NEU-021) are stored with the snapshot.

xp.title: Snapshot identity and format
xp.sources: ip-requirements.md REQ-NEU-001; Graph-Neurons-requirements.md GN-005, plan §2 ref-2026-10
xp.issue: IP exports daily Parquet snapshots for three graph levels; GN-005 uses content-addressed snapshot ids and a frozen reference snapshot.
xp.proposal: Snapshot id = GN-005 content hash. The REQ-NEU-001 Parquet export is written under that id with metadata (graph_version, recorded_at, counts). ref-2026-10 remains frozen; new snapshots never overwrite it.

xp.title: Libraries needed by IP inventions are not in the GN licence table
xp.sources: Graph-Neurons-requirements.md §1.3 ('Any dependency not in this table requires a Legal check'); ip-requirements.md REQ-NEU-001 (Parquet), REQ-INV6-003 (DP-SGD, e.g. Opacus), REQ-INV8-002 (VAR/Granger), REQ-INV7-002 (Cox model), REQ-SAS-001 (local NLI model), REQ-NEU-032 (MLflow option)
xp.issue: Parquet I/O, DP-SGD, VAR/Granger tests, Cox survival models and local NLI/extraction models need packages or model weights outside the N0–N3 table.
xp.proposal: Before use, add each package (and each model weight with its licence) to the GN licence table with tier and verdict after Legal review; record the DR id in the ledger. Until then the dependent requirement stays BLOCKED.

xp.title: Fact leases vs worker leases
xp.issue: Both programmes use the word lease: IP fact leases (default max 24 h) and ASPEII worker leases (30 s, fencing tokens).
xp.proposal: Pre-resolved by aspeii-reqirements.md §2.1: they stay separate; admission checks both where applicable; a fact TTL never extends a worker lease.

xp.title: One change stream for leases, CTAR and revocation
xp.sources: ip-requirements.md REQ-LSE-001..003; community-ip-requirements.md CIP-RQ-004, CIP-RQ-009; aspeii-reqirements.md ASPEII-RQ-030.C03
xp.issue: IP builds a graph change publisher with a transactional outbox; CIP builds durable mutation/event processing for CTAR; ASPEII invalidates admission on change. Three outboxes would disagree about ordering.
xp.proposal: One transactional outbox publishes `kgf.graph.changed` (REQ-LSE-001). CIP adds the non-graph change kinds (access, policy, prompt, model, tool, evaluator) to the same outbox with the CIP-RQ-005 metadata. Lease revocation, CTAR intake and ASPEII admission invalidation are consumers of that one stream. Synchronous read denial on revocation (CIP-RQ-009) does not wait for any consumer.

xp.title: Undeclared or unknown action class
xp.issue: IP treats an undeclared action as IRREVERSIBLE (human approval path). ASPEII says unknown effects are R4 and denied; IRREVERSIBLE does not qualify an unknown operation.
xp.proposal: Apply the stricter rule: an undeclared action is IRREVERSIBLE in the IP checkpoint and, for ASPEII-enabled effects, R4-denied with no approval path until the tool declares its action class.

xp.title: Answer checkpoint 'never blocked'
xp.issue: IP says the answer checkpoint is never blocked; ASPEII requires privacy, authorization and egress guards to still apply.
xp.proposal: Interpret 'never blocked' as never blocked because of weak epistemic status only. Authorization, derivation-guard, privacy and egress checks still withhold content at the answer checkpoint.

xp.title: Feature flags vs mandatory admission
xp.issue: REQ-SDK-002 lets `ip.warrant.enabled=false` bypass checkpoints and REQ-PLT-010 restores pre-feature behaviour; ASPEII says a legacy flag cannot bypass ASPEII admission for ASPEII-enabled effects.
xp.proposal: Flag-off restores pre-feature IP behaviour for IP features only. ASPEII admission for ASPEII-enabled effects is independent of every `ip.*` flag. The kill-switch control (IP §17.3) runs with ASPEII effects disabled.

xp.title: Evidence locations and one consolidated ledger
xp.issue: Each programme stores evidence somewhere different.
xp.proposal: Keep every native location. The consolidated ledger `docs/programme/programme-ledger.json` (schema eoip-programme-ledger-v1) records, per item, the native path and its SHA-256 digest. verify_programme_ledger.py recomputes the digests.

xp.title: Graph Neurons pre-existing test-file count (302 vs 239)
xp.sources: Graph-Neurons-requirements.md §0.5 (302); Graph-Neurons-implementation-plan.md Phase 1 gate (302) and §7 sign-off (239)
xp.issue: The plan uses two different counts for the same pre-existing suite.
xp.proposal: Neither number is assumed. Count `find tests -name "test_*.py" | wc -l` at the Phase 0a baseline, record the number and the file list digest in the GN-010 ledger, and use that recorded number for GN-PH1.G05 and GN-SO-16.

xp.title: GN-705 and GN-706 have no phase
xp.sources: Graph-Neurons-implementation-plan.md §1 phase list; Graph-Neurons-requirements.md GN-705, GN-706
xp.issue: The phase list omits GN-705 (budgets) and GN-706 (failure-mode guards), but the Phase 2 gate checks GN-706 and GN-007 uses GN-705 budgets.
xp.proposal: GN-706 belongs to Phase 2 (its gate already checks it). GN-705 is cross-phase: each budget row is measured in the phase that introduces the operation and the GN-705 ledger closes at final sign-off.

xp.title: 'A missed threshold honestly reported is complete' vs P0 must pass
xp.issue: The plan accepts an honest FAILED ledger as a completed requirement; the completion definition requires every P0 requirement to pass V2–V7.
xp.proposal: An honest FAILED ledger resolves a requirement only where the requirement text allows that outcome (GN-103, 104, 201, 202, 302, 303, 402, 403, 502, 601, 702). A FAILED P0 requirement is recorded honestly and blocks programme completion (Phase 1 'stop and escalate').

xp.title: IP: 'six' governance processes vs nine
xp.issue: Text says six processes; §15 defines nine (REQ-PRC-007..009 were added in v1.1).
xp.proposal: Nine processes. WP-24 builds REQ-PRC-001..006; WP-27, WP-28 and WP-29 build REQ-PRC-007, 008 and 009; screen 18.12 lists all nine.

xp.title: IP demo tenant id
xp.sources: ip-requirements-implementation-plan.md §4 (no id), WP-01 task 12 and WP-06/07/09 (`acme-demo`)
xp.issue: §4 never names the primary seeded tenant; later WPs call it `acme-demo`.
xp.proposal: Primary seeded tenant id is `acme-demo`; isolation tenant is `beta-demo`.

xp.title: Branching and commits: CIP forbids without authorisation, IP prescribes
xp.issue: CIP agents may not commit or create branches without authorisation; IP agents must create one branch per WP.
xp.proposal: Before CIP code work starts, the owner records whether CIP work may branch and commit (and the naming scheme, e.g. `cip/P<n>-<name>`). Until then CIP work stays in Phase 0 (documentation and inventory).

xp.title: External model endpoints
xp.sources: ip-requirements-implementation-plan.md §1.1 rule 4; ip-requirements.md REQ-PLT-005; Graph-Neurons-requirements.md GN-203 constraint 4; aspeii-implementation-plan.md §11 (hosted model profile)
xp.issue: The IP plan forbids external model calls outright; REQ-PLT-005 allows them when tenant policy permits; GN-203 and the ASPEII hosted-model profile describe configured external LLMs.
xp.proposal: Default local everywhere. An external endpoint is used only when all hold: tenant data-sharing policy permits the data class for that endpoint (REQ-PLT-005), egress controls in packages/eoip/egress/ apply (GN-203), and the ASPEII hosted-model profile has an approved budget. IP features ship and are evidenced in local mode only.

xp.title: Signing keys and trusted-key policy
xp.issue: IP gives each tenant an Ed25519 key; ASPEII signs receipts and checkpoints with managed keys and a trusted-key manifest.
xp.proposal: One signer service and one trusted-key manifest; IP tenant keys are entries in it. Rotation and revocation follow ASPEII-RQ-022 clause 2.

xp.title: Referenced documents not in this package
xp.sources: aspeii-reqirements.md header and §2 (aspeii-research-analysis.md, GUI-UIX-requirements.md, CRAr.md); Graph-Neurons-requirements.md §1.3 (ontology-competitive-analysis.md §8.1)
xp.issue: aspeii-research-analysis.md and GUI-UIX-requirements.md were not supplied. CRAr.md and ontology-competitive-analysis.md exist from the earlier CRAr package.
xp.proposal: ASPEII WP01 needs aspeii-research-analysis.md (AS-G01..G03 probes). Until supplied, WP01 gate stays BLOCKED; the probes listed in aspeii-implementation-plan.md §2.1 are the only probe definitions an agent may use.

xp.title: Retention settings
xp.issue: Three programmes touch retention.
xp.proposal: Pre-resolved by aspeii-reqirements.md §2.1: reuse the IP key; production deployments acknowledge effective retention explicitly; CIP purge and legal hold apply to warrants as to any artifact.

xp.title: Dissent diversity vs evidentiary independence
xp.issue: IP diversity uses model family; ASPEII says two models reading one source are not independent.
xp.proposal: Pre-resolved by aspeii-reqirements.md §2.1: keep the IP diversity check and also evaluate source-lineage independence for evidence.

xp.title: Commitment fulfilment evidence
xp.issue: IP fulfils a commitment with a warrant of status ≥ ATTESTED; ASPEII requires verified task outcomes.
xp.proposal: Pre-resolved by aspeii-reqirements.md §2.1: when the commitment concerns an ASPEII task, the fulfilment warrant must ground on the verified outcome record.

xp.title: Federated learning consent
xp.issue: GN forbids cross-tenant parameter sharing unless federation is enabled per tenant with recorded consent; IP Invention 6 is opt-in per tenant and data class.
xp.proposal: The REQ-INV6-001 opt-in record (who, when, which classes) is the GN-703 consent record; GN-703 tests treat a tenant without that record as non-federated.
